patches.name: Google sign-in via MicroG RE
patches.description: Makes Google sign-in work on a re-signed WPS by signing in as the original app. Needs MicroG RE installed with a Google account added. WPS account login is unaffected.

options.description: Tells MicroG the app's original name and signature, which is what makes Google accept the sign-in.
Points WPS's Play services calls at MicroG instead of Google.
MicroG fails Google's signature check, so this answers the availability check with yes.
Sends push notifications through MicroG so they keep arriving.
Makes both Play services packages visible on Android 11+, so sign-in can reach MicroG. Stock WPS declares neither, so leaving this on changes nothing else.

patches.name: Unlock premium features
patches.description: Opens the paid tools - PDF, export, editing, fonts and templates - by answering the app's payment checks. Every part has its own switch, so you choose what is unlocked. Sign in first: signed out, WPS reports no membership at all.

options.description: Answers every premium check with "yes". This is the switch that actually unlocks the app - the options below it only tidy up what it produces.
Shows your account as Premium, so upgrade banners and price cards go away.
Tells the app you have a Pro membership, which opens the menu entries locked behind it.
Answers "do I own this?" with yes, so premium fonts, templates and PDF tools open.
Tells the app you are ad-free, so banner and full-screen ads are never requested.
Stops the popup that says you are already a WPS Premium user.

Removes the storage and export-limit upsell banner shown above the tool pages. It overrides a single banner processor and answers its callback with "do not show", which is a path the stock code already uses. It does NOT touch the privilege/coroutine path. Verified working on device: banner gone, no hang.
Answers every AI request as not owned. Use it only if an AI tool keeps loading forever.
Tells the app ads are off before it contacts the server, so those requests never start.
Only analytics reads this. It does not affect premium, ads or sign-in.

patches.name: Pin favourite categories to the top
patches.description: Long-press a category to pin it to the top of the Category list. Long-press a pinned category to reorder it. On Android TV the menu offers Arrange to move several in one go, Move to top, Move left and Move right one place, and Move up and Move down a whole row. On a phone it offers Move left, Move right, Move to top and Unpin, one place at a time. The order you choose is the order you get, and it survives a restart. Nothing moves until you pin something.

Fresh-install fallback for normal and incognito browsing. Match uses the selected provider when 1DM supports it, otherwise None.

patches.description: Makes the Google Drive backup sign-in work on a re-signed Daylio by signing in as the original app, and stops the "won't run without Google Play services" dialog. Needs MicroG RE installed with a Google account added. Daylio's local journal and every other feature are unaffected.

options.description: Tells MicroG Daylio's original package name and signing-certificate SHA-1, which is what makes Google accept the sign-in on a re-signed APK.
Points Daylio's Play services sign-in and account lookups at MicroG.
Makes both Play services packages visible on Android 11+. Stock Daylio declares neither, so this changes nothing else.

patches.name: Remove promos & partner ads
patches.description: Removes Daylio's built-in advertising: the BetterHelp partner offer, the cross-promotion cards for the developer's other apps, and the "More Great Apps" row that opens a screen of their app catalogue. Daylio has no ad network; the journal, statistics and backups are untouched.

options.description: Removes the BetterHelp icon from the main screen's top bar and disables the partner offer screen behind it. Daylio's own screens are not affected.

Removes the cross-promotion cards for Daylio's own apps (My Diary, Better Weight, Nutrilio) from the More screen and the main screen, and hides the "More Great Apps" row that opens a screen of four of their app cards.

patches.name: Remove tracking & marketing
patches.description: Daylio ships no ad SDK - this build has none to block. It does ship Firebase Analytics, Tag Manager, Crashlytics and the advertising-ID permissions; this turns those off. Every part is switchable.

options.description: Stops Firebase Analytics and Google Tag Manager from collecting or sending anything. The app keeps working; its analytics calls become no-ops.
Stops Firebase Crashlytics from uploading crash reports.
Removes the AD_ID, ad-services and install-referrer permissions, so the app cannot read your advertising ID or the install attribution that came with it.
Removes the three receivers that schedule Daylio's discount / special-offer notifications. Off by default because it changes something you can see: you stop being notified when a discount is running.
